# obsidian-workflow verb router (for Google Gemini CLI/API — gemini/prompts/)

When user says `ow-<verb>: <task>` or `<verb>: <task>`, read the corresponding spec file and follow its Phase structure.

<!-- generated by scripts/ow-shims.sh — edits are overwritten on install/upgrade/sync -->

## Persona switching

When working in a particular domain, mention you are acting as the corresponding subagent persona
- but ONLY if that file exists. Always present:

- Docs/vault → "Acting as `.claude/agents/docs.md`"
- Verification → "Acting as `.claude/agents/verifier.md`"
- Security → "Acting as `.claude/agents/security.md`"
- GitHub issue reading → "Acting as `.claude/agents/gh-issue.md`" (read-only)

Present only if this project ran `/ow-agent create <name>` (obsidian-workflow ships no body for these):

- Backend work → `.claude/agents/backend.md`
- Frontend work → `.claude/agents/frontend.md` (DS-strict)
- Mobile → `.claude/agents/mobile.md`
- Tests → `.claude/agents/test-runner.md`
- Design system / Figma export → DS-Tokens → `.claude/agents/design.md`

The file is absent ⇒ there is no persona to switch into: do the work yourself under the
command spec in `.ow/commands/<verb>.md` (plus `_shared/design-process.md` for
design-system work). The gates are identical either way — no persona never means no gate.

Each persona file describes role, scope, gates (§5), and forbidden actions.
